how: the headline as written: 'the bit is exchanged ONLY by an antiunitary'. On main's own matrices the unitary S6, of determinant +1, exchanges the two ground modes exactly (overlap 1.000000): S M S^-1 = M^-1, so S6 carries the transport to its inverse and the eigenvector at +pi/6 to the one at -pi/6. Over the whole group generated by T6 and S6 (576 elements up to phases) twelve unitary elements exchange the pair and twelve antiunitary ones do (checks/sm_c18_to_c21.py, C2 and C3)
note: WHAT HOLDS IN ITS PLACE, computed on main: an element exchanges the pair exactly when it reverses the orientation of the bundle, counting both the fibre and the direction of the act. Unitaries that keep the transport keep the pair (12); unitaries that invert it exchange the pair (12); antiunitaries that keep it exchange the pair (12, the tick among them); antiunitaries that invert it keep the pair (12). So the seat's conclusion, that the bit is the hand, stands in a sharper form, and with a consequence it does not draw: the figure-eight has an orientation-reversing symmetry of its own, so the object cannot fix the sign.
